fatal_errors: The proposed iron-based BCC-to-FCC alloying strategy does not identify the target Re-containing NbMoTaW refractory high-entropy-alloy film.
It omits helium implantation and the relevant irradiation-hardening and grain-boundary-embrittlement context.
The claimed mechanism does not match the target mechanism involving grain refinement, amorphous grain-boundary regions, defect sinks, and suppression of helium-bubble segregation.
Aluminum does not generally promote an FCC structure in iron and may stabilize BCC/ferritic phases, so grouping it with nickel is scientifically unreliable.
explanation: The hypothesis addresses ductility only in a broad sense and proposes a generic FCC/slip-system argument unrelated to the target comparison between NbMoTaW and NbMoTaWRe films under room-temperature helium irradiation. It reconstructs neither the material, intervention, conditions, structural mediator, nor baseline. The predicted increase in ductility is only tangentially related to the observed reduction in irradiation-induced embrittlement. Tensile testing across alloy concentrations could test the submitted hypothesis, but the experiment lacks phase characterization and treats Ni and Al as equivalent FCC promoters. Overall, it is unsupported as a reconstruction and is also weakened by the inaccurate aluminum claim.
